ideas.hypothesis: Adopting an inflation target moves the short-term interest rate into a persistent low-volatility regime: after adoption, the estimated probability of staying in the high-volatility regime falls and the transition probabilities shift toward the low-volatility state.

sources.role: method: a regime-switching univariate diffusion model with time-varying transition probabilities for the short rate
setting and mechanism: the Canadian inflation target zone and evidence that markets form beliefs about the target band

ideas.test: Estimate a two-regime switching diffusion on weekly 3-month treasury bill rates for Canada (and one or two other early adopters such as New Zealand and the UK) from 1975 to 2007. Let the transition probabilities depend on a post-adoption dummy and compare regime persistence and volatility before and after adoption, using a non-adopter (US) as a control series.
ideas.disconfirming: The post-adoption dummy has no significant effect on the transition probabilities, or the share of time spent in the low-volatility regime rises just as much in the non-targeting control country.

ideas.hypothesis: When surrenders depend on the gap between new-money rates and crediting rates, interest-indexed annuities have markedly more negative convexity and shorter effective duration in high-volatility interest-rate regimes. A single-regime rate model therefore misstates asset-liability hedge ratios.

sources.role: mechanism and measure: a logit surrender model driven by the rate spread, used to compute annuity value, duration and convexity
method: an estimated high/low volatility regime-switching short-rate model

ideas.test: Fit the logit surrender model to one insurer's policy-level surrender data (or published industry surrender tables) and plug it into a Monte Carlo annuity valuation under (i) a single-regime short-rate model and (ii) the regime-switching model estimated on 3-month T-bill rates. Compare effective duration and convexity by starting regime.
ideas.disconfirming: Convexity and duration estimates differ by less than a small, economically trivial amount between regimes and between the single-regime and switching models.

ideas.hypothesis: Metropolitan areas whose income-based 'affordable price' is more sensitive to nominal mortgage rates, because median incomes are low relative to prices, have higher house price volatility. Nominal rate shocks pass through more strongly there.

sources.role: measure and mechanism: an 'intrinsic' house value built from local median income and prevailing nominal interest rates
mechanism: the link between interest rate levels, including very low rates, and asset prices

ideas.test: For 100 or more US metropolitan areas, build quarterly affordable-price series from median household income and the 30-year mortgage rate, and compute each metro's elasticity of affordable price to the rate. Regress the standard deviation of house price growth (FHFA index) on this elasticity, controlling for supply elasticity and employment volatility.
ideas.disconfirming: Metro-level rate sensitivity of affordable price is unrelated or negatively related to house price volatility once supply elasticity and employment volatility are controlled for.

ideas.hypothesis: The cost disadvantage of the Help to Buy equity loan relative to a conventional high loan-to-value mortgage widens as mortgage rates fall. At low rates the equity share of house price appreciation costs more than the extra interest on a larger mortgage.

sources.role: finding: first-time buyers may find it cheaper to avoid the Help to Buy equity loan
mechanism: interest rates feed into affordable prices and house price growth, which drives the cost of an equity share

ideas.test: Build a cost-comparison model for a representative first-time buyer in several UK regions. Compare the total five- and ten-year cost of a 5%-deposit Help to Buy purchase with a 90-95% LTV mortgage across historical mortgage rate scenarios (1% to 6%) and regional house price growth paths from Land Registry data.
ideas.disconfirming: The relative cost of Help to Buy does not vary with the mortgage rate, or the equity loan becomes relatively cheaper as rates fall.

ideas.hypothesis: Near the zero lower bound, inflation-target bands implied by the term structure become more asymmetric toward downside inflation deviations than in normal-rate periods, which reflects perceived limits on policy easing.

sources.role: method: testable term-structure restrictions that recover market-perceived inflation target bands and their asymmetry
setting: the zero lower bound and negative nominal rates as constraints on policy

ideas.test: Apply the term-structure target-zone estimation to Canadian (and Swedish or euro-area) government yield curves and inflation for two windows, 1995-2007 and 2009-2016. Compare the estimated band width and asymmetry around the official target between the two windows.
ideas.disconfirming: The implied band is equally symmetric, or skewed upward, in the zero-lower-bound window compared with the normal-rate window.

ideas.hypothesis: Credit scores affect loan interest rates in discrete steps at lender tier cutoffs rather than smoothly. After controlling for income, age and debt-to-income ratio, rates jump at tier thresholds.

sources.role: measure and setting: relationships between age, income, debt-to-income, credit scores and interest rates

ideas.test: Use loan-level auto or mortgage data with credit scores and contract rates (for example, a public mortgage performance dataset). Run a regression discontinuity at common score cutoffs (620, 660, 700, 740) with income, debt-to-income and age as covariates.
ideas.disconfirming: No discontinuity in interest rates appears at tier cutoffs, and the score-rate relation is smooth once borrower controls are included.

ideas.hypothesis: In Indian districts with more competing scheduled commercial banks, term deposit rates are higher and banks more often use depositor-favourable interest calculation methods, such as quarterly compounding.

sources.role: setting and measure: term deposit rates and calculation methods across scheduled commercial banks in India

ideas.test: Collect posted term deposit rates and compounding conventions for 1-, 2- and 3-year deposits from bank branches in a sample of 30 to 50 districts. Regress effective annual yield on a district Herfindahl index of deposits (from RBI branch statistics), with bank fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Effective deposit yields and compounding conventions do not vary with district bank concentration within the same bank.

ideas.hypothesis: Central banks that add an exchange-rate stabilization term to their interest rate rule spend more time in a high-volatility short-rate regime, because policy rates react to currency shocks as well as inflation gaps.

sources.role: mechanism: a Taylor-type rule augmented with nominal exchange rate stabilization in a small open economy with learning
method: regime-switching estimation of short-rate volatility regimes

ideas.test: Estimate regime-switching models on short-term interbank rates for 8 to 10 small open economies. Classify each economy's rule by whether the estimated policy reaction function includes a significant exchange rate term, then compare the unconditional probability of the high-volatility regime across the two groups.
ideas.disconfirming: Economies with exchange-rate-reactive rules show equal or lower high-volatility regime probabilities than pure inflation-responders.

ideas.hypothesis: In the Australian housing market, prolonged low mortgage rates raised house prices faster than incomes, increasing deposit barriers. This raised the share of young adults who remain long-term renters.

sources.role: finding: an emerging 'generation' of permanent renters in Australia
mechanism: interest rates and incomes jointly determine affordable house prices

ideas.test: Use household panel data (for example, HILDA waves 2001-2017) to model each 25-40-year-old's transition from renting to owning as a function of the state-level mortgage rate, the house price-to-income ratio, and individual income, with person fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Lower mortgage rates raise the renter-to-owner transition probability for young adults even after accounting for the price-to-income ratio, so falling rates reduce rather than increase permanent renting.

ideas.hypothesis: Among smallholder livestock farmers, higher microfinance lending rates raise default probabilities mainly after animal health shocks. Rate effects on default are therefore concentrated in drought or disease years.

sources.role: setting and finding: microfinance programmes for livestock farmers in Sudanese regions improved financial stability

ideas.test: Obtain loan records from one or two microfinance institutions serving livestock farmers in Sudan, with contract rates, repayment status and regional livestock disease or drought indicators. Estimate a logit of default on the loan rate interacted with a regional shock dummy.
ideas.disconfirming: The loan rate has no effect on default, or its effect does not differ between shock and non-shock years.
